transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-03
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees:
 - Sofia Patel, Redwood (AE)
 - Marcus Lee, Redwood (SE)
 - Priya Shah, Redwood (Solutions Engineer)
 - Daniel Moore, Ivory Capital (CTO)
 - Elena Alvarez, Ivory (Head Eng)
 - Ravi Menon, Ivory (Security Lead)
 - Tara Kim, Ivory (ML Engineer)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be rough):
Ivory Capital is exploring a 4-week POC to validate Redwood inference for document summarization in a regulated finance environment. Primary focus: security/compliance (SOC 2 / ISO), SSO/SAML + SCIM, RBAC, audit logs and KMS integration. Need throughput and latency benchmarks to validate cost and SLA. Acceptance criteria include SOC/ISO artifacts, network topology (VPC peering), p99 latency < 500ms for request size X, sustained 150-200 RPS with caching, and data retention controls. Next steps: Redwood to send compliance pack and benchmark harness; Ivory to provide representative prompt corpus and compliance checklist.

Topics covered:
 - Compliance: SOC two, ISO27001, encryption at rest and transit, K M S / H S M integration
 - Auth: SSO/S A M L, SCIM, SAML provisioning, SSO test accounts
 - Access controls: RBAC, least privilege, audit logging retention, immutable logs
 - Deployment modes: hosted API vs Dedicated/gpu pool vs Private VPC/on-prem
 - Benchmarks: p95/p99 latency goals, throughput RPS, sample token distributions, spike/burst behaviour
 - PoC logistics: timeline, success criteria, security review process

Transcript body (timestamps approximate, crude ASR, occasional errors):
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll do a quick intro from Redwood side. Marcus and Priya are here to cover the technical and benchmark pieces.
[00:12] Daniel: Hi all, thanks. Short on time today so want to focus on what we need to prove out in the POC; security is non-negotiable.
[00:20] Sofia: Yep understood. Could you, Daniel, just give us a quick overview — what systems this will touch and who signs off on acceptance?
[00:26] Daniel: Sure. We're a small compliance team but for production sign-off it's me and Ravi (security). We'll run the POC in our dev VPC, but ultimately we expect to run either Dedicated or Private VPC with KMS.
[00:40] Elena: For the workload, it's document summarization and redaction for investment memos; typical request payloads ~6–10k tokens, peaks in market close windows. Our target is to keep inference latency reasonable under peaks.
[00:54] Marcus: Got it. Quick question — Elena — when you say 6–10k tokens, are those request tokens or total token windows? That affects kernel selection and KV caching.
[01:04] Elena: Uh, request tokens per doc. We may chain calls. So KV cache matters.
[01:10] Priya: Noted. From Redwood side we support autoscaling dedicated pools and private deployment with customer-managed VPC. For POC we can provision a temporary dedicated pool in our staging region and give you VPC peering access.
[01:22] Ravi: On compliance, we need to see SOC two artifacts, ISO27001 certificate, and an audit log schema that shows immutable logging and retention policies. Also SSO — we require SAML-based SSO with SCIM provisioning, and RBAC with role separation.
[01:37] Sofia: Absolutely. We'll send our SOC 2 type 2 report and ISO certs. Note: some brand names in our docs might say Redwood Ded... uh "Redwood Dedicated" — ASR munged it.
[01:46] Marcus: On the audit logging side, we can emit per-request audit events including token usage, model version, per-route latency, and user ID. Logs can be forwarded to your SIEM via a streaming connector or S3 with object lock.
[02:00] Ravi: Do you support write-once storage for logs? We need tamper evidence for certain controls.
[02:06] Marcus: We can forward to S3 with object lock enabled or to a third-party log archive; for the private on-prem option you can keep logs inside your environment.
[02:15] Tara: For key management, do you support external KMS / H S M? We require customer-managed keys for the pilot.
[02:22] Priya: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported in Private mode; for Dedicated we can also integrate with your cloud KMS using KMS key policies. For Hosted API we have an option for envelope encryption but customer-managed keys are only for private/dedicated deployments.
[02:38] Daniel: Important: data residency — all telemetry and data must remain in our region for the POC. Can you pin instances to us-east-1?
[02:45] Marcus: Yes, we can pin region and provide dedicated capacity in a region. There may be some control-plane traffic back to Redwood for management; we'll itemize that in the network diagram.
[02:55] Elena: On the benchmarks — what metrics will you measure? We need p50/p95/p99, cold vs warm start, and cost per 1k tokens estimate. Also need a replication of our token distribution.
[03:07] Marcus: We'll provide a harness that drives representative prompts, measures latency distribution, throughput, GPU utilization, and token cost breakdown. We use a continuous batching simulator and can show impact of kv cache hit rates.
[03:20] Tara: Do you support quantized models for lower cost? That might change quality.
[03:24] Priya: We can run quantized variants; we'll include quality regression tests against your evaluation prompts as part of the POC acceptance.
[03:33] Daniel: Acceptance criteria — to be explicit: (1) Security artifacts reviewed and no open critical gaps, (2) p99 latency <= 500ms for 90% of our steady workload, (3) sustained 150 RPS with <5% error rate, (4) audit logs delivered and integrated with our SIEM, (5) KMS integration validated.
[03:52] Sofia: Good to have those spelled out. One callout — p99 500ms for 6–10k token requests is tough; depends on model size. Would you accept a tiered criteria — latency target for shorter requests and a separate target for large doc summarization?
[04:07] Elena: We can do that. Maybe p99 < 250ms for requests < 1k tokens, and p99 < 1s for the big 6–10k requests, as long as throughput aligns.
[04:18] Marcus: That seems reasonable. We'll put in two buckets and show a model-routing plan: smaller low-latency variant vs high-capacity variant for long docs.
[04:28] Ravi: On authentication — we need SAML SSO + SCIM to sync users and group-based RBAC. Also need audit trail showing which user triggered a model or route.
[04:38] Priya: We can do group-to-role mapping; logs will include user id and group. Note that depending on whether you use hosted vs private the SCIM endpoint location changes. We'll document that.
[04:50] Daniel: What's the planned timeline for the POC? We aim for a 4-week window but security review may add time.
[04:57] Sofia: Proposed schedule: Week 0 (this week) — exchange docs and workload samples; Week 1 — deploy staging dedicated pool and run initial smoke tests; Week 2 — full benchmark runs and security scan; Week 3 — remediation & re-run; Week 4 — acceptance and handoff.
[05:15] Elena: Works for us. We may need an extra week if legal needs to sign a DPA.
[05:19] Sofia: Understood. We'll prepare a DPA template and security pack.
[05:24] Ravi: A few detailed Qs: (a) Can we restrict model versions per team? (b) Do you expose per-token billing at token granularity tied to route? (c) How long do you retain raw prompts in logs?
[05:36] Marcus: (a) Yes, we support pinning model versions and rollout policies with canary. (b) We provide token-level cost breakdowns per route and per token bin. (c) Raw prompt retention is configurable; default purge is 30 days but for the POC we can set shorter retention or disable storing raw prompts, and store only hashed references for audit.
[05:55] Tara: For the benchmark harness, we need a way to simulate burst traffic at market close; do you have tooling for that?
[06:01] Marcus: We'll deliver a k6-based harness with tokenization plumbing; it supports burst windows and variable prompt length distribution. We'll also provide a script that reproduces batching patterns we use in prod.
[06:12] Daniel: Cost question — what's the expected cost for 4-week POC with Dedicated staging nodes? Rough ballpark.
[06:18] Sofia: Depends on capacity but for your workload we estimate $12k-$18k for the dedicated pool and benchmark run including reserved GPUs for the 4 weeks; we'll give a more precise estimate after we see the sample traces.
[06:29] Elena: Ok please send a quote.
[06:32] Sofia: Will do.
[06:34] [pause] 
[06:38] Priya: Quick note on audit logs: we can include an immutable id per request and cryptographic signing of logs if you want tamper-evidence. That's an add-on but doable.
[06:48] Ravi: That would be ideal, please include options.
[06:51] Sofia: We'll include object-lock and signed audit options in the security pack.
[06:55] Daniel: Final: can we get a skeleton runbook of the POC and a clear acceptance checklist?
[07:01] Marcus: Yes we'll produce a one-page acceptance checklist aligned with the criteria we discussed and a runbook describing how to run the harness and interpret metrics.
[07:10] Sofia: Great. Any other blockers?
[07:13] Elena: None from engineering.
[07:15] Tara: Security needs to vet the pack first.
[07:17] Daniel: Ok, thanks everyone. Let's reconvene to review artifacts on 2026-03-23.
[07:22] Sofia: Thanks, wrapping up — action items captured. We'll follow up in email with attachments.
[07:28] [meeting ends]
